title_en: The Journey to the West 10: The River of Sand
source_file: 连环画《西游记10：流沙河》（6-10岁）.pdf
full_text_zh:
[P1] 西游记之十
流沙河
流沙河
《西游记》之十
原著 吴承恩
改编 石峰
绘画 高同宝
轩观印潮
河北美术出版社

[P2] 内容提要
这是根据古典神话小说《西游记》第二十二回编绘的一本连环画。描述的是唐僧、悟空、八戒师徒三人去西天取经途中，在流沙河收服沙和尚的故事。

1 话说唐僧、悟空、八戒师徒三人，过了黄风岭，继续西进。这一日，来到一片平川之地。只见前面有一条大河挡住去路。

[P3] 2 唐僧在马上手指河面对悟空说：‘徒弟，你看那河，水势汹涌，一望无边，我们怎么能过去？’
3 悟空跳在空中，手搭凉篷眺望。也心惊地说：‘师父啊，老孙这双火眼金睛，白日能看千里，我观这条河少说也有八百里宽，又无船只可渡，师父要想过去，真个是难了！’

[P4] 4 唐僧长叹一声，下得马来，四下查看。发现岸边有座石碑，上面刻有“流沙河”三个大篆字，下面有四行小诗：“八百流沙河，三千弱水深。鹅毛飘不起，芦花定底沉。”
5 师徒们正在观看，忽听水中一阵哗响，钻出一个妖精，手持宝杖，十分凶丑。

[P5] 6 那个妖精一个旋风，奔上岸来，要抢唐僧。悟空慌忙把师父抱住，急登高岸，牢牢护定师父。
7 八戒放下担子，举起钉钯，直取妖精。那妖精使宝杖相迎，二人在河边大战起来。

[P6] 8 悟空在一旁观战，恨得咬牙切齿，摩拳擦掌，见八戒一时难以取胜，忍不住腾空跳起，上前就是一棒。
9 那妖精力战八戒，只打个平手，又见悟空前来助战，料难对敌，慌忙钻入流沙河。

[P7] 10 八戒气呼呼地埋怨着：‘猴哥，谁叫你来的！那妖精渐渐手慢，难以招架，再打三五回合，我就擒住他了！’悟空笑着说：‘好久不曾耍棒，心痒难耐，故尔前来，不曾想那怪怯阵逃走了。’
11 二人回到唐僧跟前，唐僧问道：‘可曾捉住妖怪？’悟空说：‘那妖败阵，钻入水中去了。’唐僧心情烦闷，说：‘妖怪逃走，流沙河难渡，怎生是好？’

[P8] 12 悟空望望流沙河，沉思片刻，对八戒说：“你水性好，下水与他去交战，许败不许胜，把他引诱出来，我下手帮你擒他。”
13 八戒说：“此计甚好，我去也！”手持钉钯，跃浪翻波，径直闯入水底。

[P9] 14 再说那妖精败阵回到水府，刚刚喘定，忽听有人推得哗哗水响，抬头一看，原来是八戒闯到跟前。
15 那妖勃然大怒：‘好你个猪嘴和尚，胆敢闯我水府，休走看杖！’八戒举钯相迎，二人又在水底争斗起来。

[P10] 16 只见钉钯上下飞舞，宝杖呼呼作响，你来我往，各显神通，斗有三四十个回合，仍不分胜负。二人踏波登浪，从水底打到了水面。
17 八戒还想恋战，忽然记起悟空言语，急忙虚幌一钯，佯输诈败，转身朝岸上奔去。妖精不知是计，紧紧追赶。

[P11] 18 刚刚到了岸边，悟空早等得不耐烦了，挥起金箍棒，冲妖精劈头就打。妖精不敢招架，慌忙转身，又钻入流沙河。
19 八戒气呼呼地埋怨说：‘你这个弼马温，真是个急猴子！再缓一会儿，等我哄他到了高处，你再拦住河边打他，叫他不能入水，岂不拿住了！他这次进去，几时才肯出来？’

[P12] 20 八戒说完，转身去见师父，悟空在后笑嘻嘻地相随。二人来到师父跟前，将方才交战情况讲了一遍。唐僧说：‘妖怪又走了，如何是好？’悟空说：‘师父放心，今日已晚，我去化些斋饭你吃，明日再设法拿妖。’
21 悟空见附近没有人家，便嘱咐八戒保护好师父，自己驾筋斗云，奔千里之外化斋去了。

[P13] 22 不大工夫，悟空返回，将斋饭献到师父面前。师徒三人用罢饭，便安歇在流沙边的高崖之上。
23 一觉醒来，天色已明。唐僧说：‘悟空，今日怎么办呢？’悟空说：‘还得让八戒下水。’

[P14] 24 八戒推辞说：‘师兄，今日你下水吧，我看护师父。’
悟空说：‘贤弟，水下功夫你比我强，不要推脱了。这回你
引诱他上来，我再也不性急了。’
25 八戒抖擞精神，手持钉钯，分开水路，又闯进水底。
那妖精刚刚睡醒，忽听得有人推得水响，急回头观看，见
八戒又来了，忙跳起身来，挥杖就打。

[P15] 26 八戒举钯架住，骂道：‘泼怪休逞强，今天叫你知道猪祖宗的厉害！’二人又大战起来。不一会又从水底打出水面。
27 二人在水面上斗了三四十个回合，还是不分胜负。八戒又使个佯输计，拖了钉钯便走。妖精随后赶来，可刚到岸边，便停了脚步。

[P16] 28 八戒在岸上骂道：‘在水里，你算什么英雄？咱两个在高岸上脚踏实地，见个高低。’妖精回骂道：‘你是哄我上去，叫你那个帮手打我哩！我不会再上当了。’
29 悟空见那妖精学乖了，再不肯上岸，急得抓耳挠腮，恨不得一把捉来。他使了个‘饿鹰扑食’的手段，急纵筋斗跳在半空，刷地落下来，要抓那妖精。

[P17] 30 妖精正与八戒吵嚷，忽听得头顶风响，急抬头，见是悟空落下，慌忙扎下水去，隐迹潜踪，渺然不见。
31 悟空、八戒望着水面，呆立了半个时辰，不见动静，只得回转。

[P18] 32 二人到了师父面前，说知此事。唐僧闻言，连连叹息：‘西天之路，如此艰难，怎么到达？流沙河怎么渡过？’悟空劝道：‘师父，请不要过分哀伤烦恼。常言说，‘车到山前必有路。’我们可以再想办法。’
33 八戒摇摇头，摆摆手，说：‘得了吧！我们有什么办法呢？流沙河的路在哪里？’悟空上前拍拍他的脑袋，笑道：‘你嘴巴长，见识短，知道什么！现在你要仔细保护师父，我到南海走一趟。’

[P19] 34 八戒问：‘你去南海做什么？’悟空说：‘这扶保师父去西天取经的事，原本是观音菩萨引荐，今日路阻流沙河，不能前进，还得请菩萨设法相助。’唐僧说：‘如此甚好，快去快回。’
35 悟空拜别师父，急纵筋斗云，眨眼不见。唐僧、八戒遥望南天，等待佳音。

[P20] 36 不一会儿，悟空便来到南海普陀山紫竹林外。守山神将迎上前问：‘大圣到此何事？’悟空说：‘我师有难，特来拜见菩萨，烦劳通禀。’
37 观音菩萨正与捧珠龙女在宝莲池畔扶栏看花，闻听禀报，便传谕悟空进见。

[P21] 38 悟空来到朝音洞，拜见菩萨，说明来意。菩萨笑问道：‘你们与那妖怪打斗时，不曾说明是取经人吗？’悟空说：‘我们只想拿住他，叫他送我师父过河，别的不曾讲。’菩萨说：‘这就难怪他了。’
39 接着，菩萨告诉悟空：‘流沙河的妖精乃是上天卷帘大将临凡，因违犯天条，被贬流沙河。是我特意叫他在那里等候唐僧。你们若说出是东土取经人，他决不会争持，定然归顺。’

[P22] 40 悟空听了，顿时喜笑颜开，但又问道：‘那妖精如今潜踪水底，怎么叫他归顺？我师父怎么渡过流沙河？’菩萨说：‘你不必忧烦，我自有办法。’说完，从袖中取出一个红葫芦。
41 菩萨唤木叉前来，对他说：‘你同悟空到流沙河水面上，对着葫芦只叫声‘悟净’，他就出来了。然后把他项下九个骷髅取下穿在一起，按九宫排列，把这葫芦放在当中，就是法船一只，能渡唐僧过河。’

[P23] 42 木叉谨遵师命，捧着葫芦出了朝音洞，与悟空一起腾云架雾，直奔流沙河。
43 不一会儿，二人来到流沙河边，按落云头。八戒见是菩萨的大弟子木叉来到，忙引师父上前拜见。

[P24] 44 悟空把菩萨所讲的话向师父禀明，唐僧转忧为喜，对木叉躬身施礼道：“感谢菩萨恩典，想不到我在这流沙河还能收一徒弟。望请速唤悟净前来见我。”
45 木叉捧定葫芦，腾云来到流沙河半空，对水面高声叫道：“悟净，取经人在此，速来归顺！”

[P25] 46 再说那怪惧怕猴王，逃回水府，正在歇息，忽听有人叫他法名，以为是菩萨到了，慌忙钻出水面。
47 他抬头一看，见是木叉，上前施礼道：‘尊者失迎，菩萨在哪里？’木叉说：‘我师未来，特差我前来吩咐，用你项上骷髅和这个葫芦，结成一只法船，渡取经人过河。’

[P26] 48 悟净问：‘取经人在哪里？’木叉用手一指说：‘那高岸上坐的便是东土圣僧唐三藏。’悟净跳上高岸，对唐僧双膝下跪说：‘师父，弟子有眼无珠，不认得师父尊容，多有冲撞，万望恕罪。’
49 八戒在一旁说：‘你这家伙，为何早不皈依？’悟空笑道：‘这不能怪他，是我们不曾说出取经的事。’唐僧欢天喜地，上前双手扶起悟净。

[P27] 50 接着，唐僧吩咐说：‘取戒刀来，与悟净落发。’悟空依言，给他剃了头。事毕，悟净复又拜了唐僧，并拜见师兄悟空和八戒。唐僧见他行礼，很有和尚家风，故又叫他沙和尚。
51 根据菩萨的吩咐，悟净将项下挂的骷髅取下，用绳索结作九宫，把菩萨的葫芦安放其中。唐僧登上法船一试，果然稳似轻舟。

[P28] 52 左有八戒扶持，右有悟净捧托；悟空在后面牵了龙马，半云半雾相跟；头顶上又有木叉护卫，唐僧坐在法船上，箭一般驶向彼岸。
53 到达彼岸，木叉收了葫芦，那骷髅突然化作九股清风，不知去向。

[P29] 54 木叉驾起云雾，回至南海。唐僧、悟空、八戒、悟净师徒四人又踏上了取经的征途，继续向西走去。欲知后事如何，请看第十一册《万年人参果》。

full_text_en:
[P1] Journey to the West, Part Ten
The River of Flowing Sand
The River of Flowing Sand
Journey to the West, Part Ten
Original work by Wu Cheng'en
Adapted by Shi Feng
Illustrated by Gao Tongbao
Xuan Guan Yin Chao
Hebei Fine Arts Publishing House

[P2] Content Summary
This is a comic book adapted from Chapter 22 of the classical mythological novel 'Journey to the West'. It tells the story of Tang Sanzang, Wukong, and Bajie, the three disciples, on their journey to the West to obtain scriptures, and how they subdue the monk Sha at the Flowing Sand River.

1 Once upon a time, the three disciples—Tang Sanzang, Wukong, and Bajie—had passed Huangfeng Ridge and continued westward. One day, they arrived at a vast plain. They saw a great river blocking their path ahead.

[P3] 2 Tang Sanzang, sitting on his horse, points at the river and says to Wukong: 'Disciple, look at that river. The water is surging, boundless as far as the eye can see. How can we possibly cross it?'
3 Wukong leaps into the air, shading his eyes with his hand to look around. He says, alarmed: 'Master, with my fiery eyes that can see a thousand miles in broad daylight, I estimate this river is at least eight hundred li wide. There are no boats to ferry us across. It will truly be difficult for you to cross, Master!'

[P4] 4 The monk sighed deeply, dismounted from his horse, and looked around. He found a stone tablet by the shore, engraved with the three large seal characters "Liu Sha He" (Flowing Sand River), and below them, four lines of small poetry: "Eight hundred li of Flowing Sand River, three thousand li of weak water deep. A goose feather cannot float, a reed flower sinks to the bottom." 
5 As the disciples were watching, suddenly a loud splash came from the water, and a demon emerged, holding a magic staff, looking extremely fierce and ugly.

[P5] 6 The demon, in a whirlwind, rushed ashore to seize Tang Sanzang. Wukong hurriedly grabbed his master, quickly climbed to a high bank, and firmly protected him.
7 Bajie put down his burden, raised his rake, and charged at the demon. The demon met him with his magic staff, and the two engaged in a fierce battle by the riverbank.

[P6] 8 Wukong watched the battle from the side, gnashing his teeth and rubbing his fists, seeing Baijie struggling to win. He couldn't hold back any longer, leaped into the air, and rushed forward with a strike.
9 The demon fought Baijie with all his might, only managing a stalemate. Seeing Wukong come to help, he realized he couldn't win and hurriedly dived back into the Flowing Sand River.

[P7] 10 Pigsy grumbled angrily: 'Monkey Brother, who called you here! That demon is gradually slowing down, hard to fight, just a few more rounds and I would have caught him!' Wukong smiled and said: 'I haven't played with my staff for a long time, it's itching to be used, so I came over. I didn't expect that monster to flee in fear.
11 The two returned to Master Tang. Master Tang asked: 'Did you catch the demon?' Wukong said: 'That demon lost the battle and dived into the water.' Master Tang, feeling troubled, said: 'The demon has escaped, the Flowing Sand River is hard to cross, what should we do?'

[P8] 12 Wukong looked at the Flowing Sand River, thought for a moment, and said to Bajie: "You're good at swimming. Go down into the water and fight him. You may lose, but you must not win. Lure him out, and I'll come down to help you capture him."
13 Bajie said: "That's a great plan, I'm going!" Holding his rake, he leaped into the waves, splashing through the water, and plunged straight to the riverbed.

[P9] 14 After the demon retreated in defeat back to his underwater palace and had just caught his breath, he suddenly heard splashing water and looked up to see that it was Pigsy who had arrived.
15 The demon became furious: 'You pig-faced monk, how dare you intrude into my underwater palace? Don't run—here comes my staff!' Pigsy raised his rake to meet him, and the two began fighting again at the bottom of the water.

[P10] 16 The rake and the magic staff flew and clanged, as they fought back and forth, each displaying their supernatural skills. After thirty to forty rounds, they were still evenly matched. The two battled across the waves, from the riverbed up to the surface.
17 Eight-Immortal still wanted to continue fighting, but suddenly remembered Wukong's words. He quickly feinted with his rake, pretended to lose, and turned to run toward the shore. The demon, unaware of the trick, chased after him tightly.

[P11] 18 Just as they reached the shore, Wukong, who had been waiting impatiently, swung his golden cudgel and struck the demon head-on. The demon dared not fight back, hastily turned around, and dived back into the Flowing Sand River.
19 Bajie grumbled angrily: 'You, you弼马温 (Bì Mǎ Wēn), are truly an impatient monkey! Just wait a little longer. Let me lure him to a high place, then you block him at the riverbank and hit him, preventing him from entering the water—wouldn't we have caught him then? He went in this time; when will he come out?'

[P12] 20 After speaking, Bajie turned to see his master, with Wukong following behind, smiling. The two came before the master and recounted the details of their recent battle. Tang僧 said, 'The demon has fled again. What shall we do?' Wukong replied, 'Master, don't worry. It's late today. I'll go beg some food for you to eat, and tomorrow we'll find a way to capture the demon.'
21 Wukong saw no houses nearby, so he instructed Bajie to protect the master, then rode his cloud of somersaults, flying thousands of miles away to beg for food.

[P13] 22 After a short while, Wukong returned and presented the meal to his master. The master and his two disciples finished their meal and then rested on a high cliff by the Flowing Sand River.
23 Upon waking, the sky was already bright. Tang僧 said: 'Wukong, what shall we do today?' Wukong replied: 'We still need to send Bajie into the water.'

[P14] 24 Pigsy hesitated and said, 'Brother, you go into the water today. I'll guard Master.'
Wukong said, 'Younger brother, you are better at underwater skills than I am. Don't hesitate. This time, you lure him up, and I won't be in such a hurry anymore.'
25 Pigsy rallied his spirit, held his rake, parted the water, and plunged into the riverbed again.
The demon had just woken up, when suddenly he heard the sound of someone pushing through the water. He quickly turned to look and saw Pigsy had come again. He jumped up immediately and swung his staff to attack.

[P15] 26 Pigsy raised his rake to block, shouting, 'You wretched demon, stop showing off! Today I'll show you the might of the Pig Ancestor!' The two engaged in battle again. In no time, they fought their way back up from the riverbed to the surface.
27 The two fought for thirty to forty rounds on the water's surface, still evenly matched. Pigsy then used a feigned retreat, dragging his rake and running away. The demon followed closely, but as soon as he reached the riverbank, he stopped in his tracks.

[P16] 28 Pigsy shouted from the shore: 'In the water, what kind of hero are you? Let's settle this on solid ground, you and I, and see who's better.' The demon retorted: 'You're trying to lure me up there so your helper can attack me! I won't fall for it again.'
29 Wukong saw that the demon had become cautious and refused to come ashore. He became frantic, scratching his ears and pulling at his cheeks, wishing he could seize the demon in one go. He used the technique 'Hunger Eagle Plunging for Prey,' leaping into the air with a swift somersault, then dropping down suddenly to grab the demon.

[P17] 30 The demon was arguing with Eight戒 when suddenly he heard a wind rushing from above. He quickly looked up and saw Wukong descending. In panic, he dived back into the water, disappearing without a trace.
31 Wukong and Eight戒 stared at the water's surface, standing motionless for half a time period, seeing no movement, and had no choice but to turn back.

[P18] 32 The two arrived before their master and told him what had happened. Tang Sanzang, upon hearing this, sighed repeatedly: 'The path to the West is so difficult—how can we reach it? How can we cross the Flowing Sand River?' Wukong advised: 'Master, please do not grieve too much. As the saying goes, “When the cart reaches the mountain, there will be a path.” We can think of another way.
33 Bajie shook his head and waved his hands, saying: 'Enough! What can we do? Where is the path across the Flowing Sand River?' Wukong stepped forward, patted his head, and laughed: 'You have a long mouth and short sight—what do you know! Now you must carefully protect the master. I will go to the South Sea for a while.'

[P19] 34 Pigsy asks: 'What are you going to do in the South Sea?' Wukong replies: 'This mission of escorting the Master to fetch scriptures in the West was originally recommended by Bodhisattva Guanyin. Today, we are blocked by the Flowing Sand River and cannot proceed. We must ask the Bodhisattva to help us find a way.' Tang Sanzang says: 'That's very good, go quickly and return quickly.'
35 Wukong bids farewell to his Master, swiftly rides the Cloud of the Somersault, and vanishes in an instant. Tang Sanzang and Pigsy gaze toward the southern sky, waiting for good news.

[P20] 36 After a while, Wukong arrived at the outskirts of the Purple Bamboo Grove on Mount Putuo in the South Sea. A mountain guardian deity stepped forward and asked, 'Great Sage, what brings you here?' Wukong replied, 'My master is in trouble. I have come to pay respects to the Bodhisattva. Please inform her for me.'
37 The Bodhisattva Guanyin was with the Dragon Maiden holding pearls, leaning on the railing by the Precious Lotus Pond to admire the flowers. Upon hearing the report, she ordered Wukong to be admitted.

[P21] 38 Wukong arrived at the Cave of the Sound of the Dharma, paid respects to the Bodhisattva, and explained his purpose. The Bodhisattva smiled and asked, 'When you fought that demon, didn't you tell him you were the pilgrim from the East?' Wukong replied, 'We only wanted to capture him and make him ferry my master across the river; we didn't mention anything else.' The Bodhisattva said, 'That's why he resisted.'
39 Then, the Bodhisattva told Wukong, 'The demon of the Flowing Sand River is actually the Heavenly Curtain-Roller General, who was banished to the Flowing Sand River for violating heavenly laws. I specifically sent him there to wait for Tang Sanzang. If you tell him you are the pilgrim from the East, he will not resist and will surely submit.'

[P22] 40 Wukong, upon hearing this, smiled with joy, but then asked: 'That demon is now hiding beneath the water. How can we make him submit? How will my master cross the Flowing Sand River?' The Bodhisattva said: 'Don't worry, I have a plan.'说完, from her sleeve, she took out a red gourd.
41 The Bodhisattva called forth Mu Cha and said to him: 'You and Wukong go to the surface of the Flowing Sand River. Call out 'Wujing' toward the gourd, and he will come out. Then take the nine skulls from around his neck, string them together, arrange them in the Nine Palaces formation, place this gourd in the center, and it will become a magical boat capable of ferrying the monk across the river.'

[P23] 42 Mu Cha, obeying his master's command, carried the gourd out of the Chao Yin Cave and flew with Wukong, riding the clouds and mist, straight to the Flowing Sand River.
43 In no time, the two arrived at the bank of the Flowing Sand River and landed. Bajie, seeing that the Great Disciple of the Bodhisattva, Mu Cha, had arrived, hurriedly led the Master forward to pay respects.

[P24] 44 Wukong reported to his master what the Bodhisattva had said. Tang Sanzang, now reassured, bowed to Mu Cha and said, "Thank you, Bodhisattva, for your grace. I never thought I would be able to take on a disciple here at the Flowing Sand River. Please quickly summon Wujing to come and see me."
45 Mu Cha held the gourd firmly, flew to the middle of the Flowing Sand River, and shouted loudly toward the water: "Wujing, the scripture-fetcher is here! Come and submit quickly!"

[P25] 46 The monster, fearing the Monkey King, fled back to his underwater palace and was resting when suddenly he heard someone calling his Dharma name. Thinking it was the Bodhisattva, he hurriedly surfaced.
47 He looked up and saw Mu Cha. He bowed respectfully and said, 'Respected one, I apologize for not greeting you properly. Where is the Bodhisattva?' Mu Cha replied, 'My master has not yet arrived. He has sent me to instruct you: use the skulls on your neck and this gourd to form a magic boat to ferry the pilgrim across the river.'

[P26] 48 Wujing asked, 'Where is the scripture seeker?' Mu Cha pointed and said, 'The one sitting on the high bank is the Eastern Sage, Tang Sanzang.' Wujing jumped onto the high bank and knelt before Tang Sanzang, saying, 'Master, your disciple is blind and failed to recognize your noble appearance. I have caused much offense; I beg for your forgiveness.'
49 Bajie said beside him, 'You fellow, why didn't you submit earlier?' Wukong smiled and said, 'We can't blame him; it's because we never mentioned our journey to fetch scriptures.' Tang Sanzang was overjoyed and stepped forward to help Wujing up with both hands.

[P27] 50 Then, Master Tang instructed: 'Bring the monk's knife and shave Wujing's head.' Sun Wukong obeyed and shaved his head. Afterward, Wujing bowed to Master Tang again and greeted his elder brothers, Wukong and Baijie. Seeing his respectful manners, Master Tang thought he had the bearing of a true monk, so he called him Sha Monk.
51 Following the Bodhisattva's instructions, Wujing took down the skulls hanging around his neck, tied them with ropes into a nine-grid pattern, and placed the Bodhisattva's gourd inside. Master Tang stepped onto the magic boat to test it, and it was indeed as steady as a light boat.

[P28] 52 On the left, Bajie supports; on the right, Wujing holds up; Wukong follows behind leading the dragon horse, half-cloud, half-mist; above, Mu Cha guards; Tang Sanzang sits on the magic boat, speeding like an arrow toward the other shore.
53 Upon reaching the other shore, Mu Cha retrieves the gourd, and the skulls suddenly transform into nine gusts of clear wind, vanishing without a trace.

[P29] 54 Mu Cha rode on clouds and mist, returning to the South Sea. Master Tang, Wukong, Baijie, and Wujing, the four disciples, once again set out on their journey to obtain scriptures, continuing westward. To learn what happens next, please read Volume Eleven, 'The Ten-Thousand-Year Ginseng Fruit'.

full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为《西游记》之十《流沙河》的封面，展示了唐僧师徒四人与沙僧相遇的场景，并列出了原著作者、改编者、绘画者及出版社信息。
[P2] 本页为《西游记》连环画《流沙河》的内容提要，介绍了故事背景，并以第一幅图画和文字描述了唐僧师徒三人过黄风岭后，来到一片平川，被一条大河挡住去路的情景。
[P3] 唐僧师徒三人被一条汹涌宽阔的大河挡住去路，唐僧向孙悟空询问如何渡河，孙悟空腾空眺望后，也感到为难，称河宽八百里且无船可渡。
[P4] 唐僧师徒在流沙河边发现刻有警示诗句的石碑，随后水中钻出一个手持宝杖、凶丑的妖精。
[P5] 妖精从水中冲上岸欲抢唐僧，孙悟空急忙护住师父；随后猪八戒放下担子，与妖精在河边展开激战。
[P6] 孙悟空见猪八戒与妖怪交战难分胜负，便上前助战，妖怪见势不妙，慌忙逃入流沙河中。
[P7] 猪八戒埋怨孙悟空插手战斗，认为自己本可擒住妖怪；孙悟空解释自己因手痒才出手，妖怪已逃入水中。二人回到唐僧面前，唐僧因妖怪逃走、渡河无望而忧心忡忡。
[P8] 孙悟空与猪八戒商议对策，让猪八戒下水引诱妖怪，自己在岸上接应；猪八戒随即持钉耙跃入流沙河中。
[P9] 妖精败退回水府后，猪八戒追入水中，妖精大怒，二人在水底再次展开激战。
[P10] 猪八戒与流沙河妖精在水底激战数十回合不分胜负，随后猪八戒佯装败退引诱妖精追赶，为孙悟空在岸上接应创造机会。
[P11] 孙悟空在岸边见到妖怪刚上岸，便立即挥棒攻击，妖怪慌忙逃回流沙河；猪八戒对此不满，埋怨孙悟空太急躁，认为应等他将妖怪引到高处再围攻。
[P12] 猪八戒和孙悟空向唐僧汇报与妖怪交战的情况，唐僧担忧妖怪逃脱；孙悟空安慰师父并决定去化斋，随后驾筋斗云飞走。
[P13] 孙悟空化斋归来，师徒三人用饭后在流沙河边的高崖上安歇；次日清晨，唐僧询问对策，孙悟空提议让猪八戒再次下水。
[P14] 猪八戒推辞下水，孙悟空劝他不要推脱并承诺不再性急；随后猪八戒再次潜入水底，妖怪刚睡醒便发现他，立即起身挥杖攻击。
[P15] 猪八戒与流沙河妖精在水底激战后再次浮出水面，二人在水面上大战三四十回合不分胜负，猪八戒佯装败退引诱妖怪追赶，妖怪追至岸边时突然停步。
[P16] 猪八戒在岸边挑衅妖怪，邀其上岸决斗，妖怪识破计谋拒绝上岸；孙悟空见状急躁，施展‘饿鹰扑食’从空中扑向妖怪。
[P17] 孙悟空从空中扑向妖怪，妖怪慌忙潜入水中逃走；孙悟空与猪八戒在岸边等待许久未见动静，只得返回。
[P18] 猪八戒和孙悟空向唐僧汇报与妖怪交战未果的情况，唐僧忧心如何渡河；孙悟空劝慰师父后，决定独自前往南海寻求帮助。
[P19] 孙悟空向唐僧和猪八戒说明要去南海请观音菩萨相助渡河，随后拜别师父驾筋斗云飞走，唐僧和猪八戒在岸边遥望等待消息。
[P20] 孙悟空来到南海普陀山紫竹林外，向守山神将说明来意，请求拜见观音菩萨；观音菩萨在宝莲池畔听闻禀报后，传令让孙悟空进见。
[P21] 孙悟空拜见观音菩萨，说明与流沙河妖怪交战未果的情况；观音菩萨指出妖怪原是天庭卷帘大将，因犯天条被贬，并告知只要说明取经身份，妖怪便会归顺。
[P22] 孙悟空向观音菩萨请教如何收服流沙河妖怪并渡河，菩萨取出红葫芦，并吩咐木叉协助，用葫芦呼唤妖怪并以九个骷髅和葫芦组成法船渡唐僧过河。
[P23] 木叉遵照观音菩萨的吩咐，带着葫芦与孙悟空一同飞往流沙河；二人抵达河边后，猪八戒认出木叉并引导唐僧上前拜见。
[P24] 孙悟空将观音菩萨的指示告知唐僧，唐僧转忧为喜并拜见木叉；木叉手持葫芦飞至流沙河上空，高声呼唤妖怪悟净前来归顺。
[P25] 流沙河妖怪因惧怕孙悟空而逃回水府歇息，忽闻有人呼唤其法名，以为是观音菩萨到来，便急忙浮出水面。他见到木叉后施礼询问菩萨下落，木叉传达观音菩萨的指令，要求他用颈上骷髅和葫芦结成法船，渡唐僧过河。
[P26] 悟净在木叉指引下认出唐僧并跪地请罪，唐僧欢喜地扶起他；八戒责问悟净为何不早皈依，悟空解释因未说明取经之事，唐僧因此高兴地接纳了悟净。
[P27] 唐僧为悟净剃度并赐名沙和尚，悟净随后按观音菩萨的吩咐，用颈上骷髅和葫芦制成法船，唐僧试乘后发现船体稳固。
[P28] 唐僧师徒乘坐由骷髅和葫芦组成的法船渡过流沙河，抵达彼岸后，木叉收回葫芦，骷髅化作清风消失。
[P29] 本页描绘了唐僧师徒四人渡过流沙河后，继续向西取经的场景。木叉返回南海，师徒四人踏上新的征程。页面下方附有《西游记》连环画的完整目录。
[P30] 本页为《西游记》连环画《流沙河》的版权页，列出了原著者、改编者、绘者、出版发行信息、ISBN及定价等出版信息。
